Download a plotly chart as a PNG, with a heading

Source: R/crukDownloadChart.R
crukDownloadChartButton.Rd

A CRUK-branded button that saves a rendered plotly chart as a PNG including a heading, without using plotly's modebar or any plotly.js export function. The browser takes a snapshot of the chart's rendered SVG with html2canvas, placed under a heading, and downloads it. Nothing is sent to or rendered by the server, so it does not need Chrome, kaleido or Python on shinyapps.io / Posit Connect.

Usage

crukDownloadChartButton(
  plotId,
  filename = "chart",
  heading = NULL,
  headingId = NULL,
  subheading = NULL,
  subheadingId = NULL,
  text = "Download chart",
  type = "secondary",
  icon = "download",
  align = "right",
  scale = 2,
  class = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

plotId

The output id of the plotly chart (the id passed to plotly::plotlyOutput()). Inside a module, pass ns("plot").

filename

File name without extension. Characters that are unsafe in file names are replaced with -.

heading

Optional fixed heading text.

headingId

Optional id of an element on the page whose text is used as the heading. Inside a module, pass ns("heading").

subheading

Optional fixed subheading text, shown under the heading in the PNG. Can be used with or without a heading.

subheadingId

Optional id of an element on the page (typically an shiny::h4()) whose text is used as the subheading. It is read at click time, like headingId. If both subheading and subheadingId are given, subheading wins. Inside a module, pass ns("subheading").

text

Button label.

type

Either "primary" (magenta background) or "secondary" (default, white background with magenta border).

icon

Optional Google Material Symbol shown after the label. One of "upload_file", "download" (default), "check_circle", "open_in_new", "content_copy", "mail" or "share". Use NULL for no icon.

align

Horizontal alignment of the button within its container, "right" (default) or "left".

scale

Resolution multiplier for the PNG. 2 gives a sharper image.

class

Optional extra CSS classes for the button.

...

Further attributes passed to the button tag.

Value

A button tag with CRUK branding and its CSS/JavaScript dependencies attached.

Details

The heading can come from an existing element on the page (headingId), from a fixed string (heading), or both. If both are given, heading wins. Use headingId when the on-screen heading is dynamic (for example a textOutput() or uiOutput() inside an shiny::h3()), because the text is read at click time.

The button is styled to match crukDownloadButton() and crukButton().

Examples

if (interactive() && requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(shiny)
  ui <- fluidPage(
    h3(id = "cars_title", "Stopping distance by speed"),
    plotly::plotlyOutput("cars"),
    crukDownloadChartButton("cars", filename = "cars", headingId = "cars_title")
  )
  server <- function(input, output, session) {
    output$cars <- plotly::renderPlotly(plotly::plot_ly(cars, x = ~speed, y = ~dist))
  }
  shinyApp(ui, server)
}
